title: Who Owns It?
rule: When one person or animal owns something, add an apostrophe and s. If there is more than one but nobody owns anything, just add s.
trickText: Ask: does someone own something? Then use an apostrophe and s, like the dog's bone. If it just means more than one, like two dogs, add only s.
say: Today's case: the apostrophe. When one person or animal owns something, we add an apostrophe and s. But when there is just more than one, we add only s. Ask yourself: does anyone own something?

example.say: The bone belongs to the dog. One owner owns something, so we write dog apostrophe s.

discover.intro: Sort these. Does someone own something, or is it just more than one?

groups.label: Someone owns something
groups.why: The apostrophe s shows who owns it.

groups.label: Just more than one
groups.why: It only means more than one, so it is just s.

discover.question: What shows that someone owns something?
discover.reveal: Yes! An apostrophe and s shows who owns something. Just s means more than one.

activities.instruction: Does someone own something? Choose apostrophe s, or just s.

items.why: One dog owns the bone, so add an apostrophe and s: dog's.
Mom owns the car, so add an apostrophe and s: Mom's.
The tail belongs to one cat, so add an apostrophe and s: cat's.
The hat belongs to Ben, so add an apostrophe and s: Ben's.
The book belongs to my sister, so add an apostrophe and s: sister's.
The nest belongs to the bird, so add an apostrophe and s: bird's.
Two means more than one, and nobody owns anything. So add just s: dogs.
Three means more than one, and nobody owns anything. So add just s: cats.
Five birds is just more than one. No owner, so just s.
Ten ducks is just more than one. No owner, so just s.
More than one book, and nobody owns anything. Just s.
More than one boy, and nobody owns anything here. Just s.
